who: James Z. Gao, historian of modern China at the University of Maryland, College Park; PhD Yale 1994.

evidence.says: Gao received his Yale PhD in 1994 and joined Maryland’s History Department in 1998.
The authority identifies James Z. Gao, also James Zheng Gao, as a history faculty member at Maryland, College Park, through The A to Z of Modern China.

notes: Institution and PhD institution/year match. The J. X. Gao candidate is associated with engineering and manufacturing, rather than this history career.

who: Jennifer L. Gaynor, historian of maritime Southeast Asia at the University at Buffalo; PhD Anthropology and History, Michigan 2005.

evidence.says: The Fall 2006 newsletter identifies Gaynor as a 2005 Michigan PhD in Anthropology and History and announces her Buffalo history appointment for Fall 2007.
The authority for Jennifer L. Gaynor cites Intertidal History in Island Southeast Asia and a 2017 publisher biography identifying her as Buffalo history faculty.
Phillip B. Guingona acknowledges Jennifer Gaynor among the University at Buffalo historians who guided his historical training.

notes: PhD and Buffalo career agree. The J. William Gaynor candidate is a surgeon in the LC record.

who: Frederick C. Giffin, historian of modern Russia and Russian-American relations at Arizona State University; PhD Emory.

evidence.says: ASU identifies Giffin as history faculty from 1967 to 2000, specializing in modern Russia, with graduate degrees in history from Emory.
The authority for Frederick C. Giffin explicitly identifies him as an Arizona State University professor emeritus of history.

notes: The faculty period includes Weidemaier’s 1975 dissertation; Emory and the Russian-history field agree. The precise PhD year was not independently confirmed.

who: Travis Glasson, historian of Britain, the British Empire and the Atlantic world at Temple University; PhD Columbia.

evidence.says: Temple identifies Glasson as a historian on its faculty since 2006 following a Columbia PhD, and lists Mastering Christianity among his books.
David W. Thomas’s December 2018 Temple dissertation, The Anxious Atlantic, names Travis Glasson as advisory chair in History.
The authority links Travis Glasson to Mastering Christianity and identifies him as Temple history faculty through Nobody Men.

notes: Direct dissertation-chair evidence, institution, doctoral institution and authored works establish the match.

who: Joshua Goldstein, historian of modern China at the University of Southern California; PhD UC San Diego, listed by USC as 2000.

evidence.says: USC lists a 2000 UC San Diego PhD in Modern Chinese History, USC faculty service since 2005, and the books Drama Kings and Everyday Modernity in China.
The 2024 PhD program names Joshua Goldstein as dissertation chair for Lina Nie’s History dissertation Going Offshore.
The Drama Kings authority cites USC’s biography identifying this Joshua Goldstein as USC faculty with a UC San Diego doctorate in modern Chinese history.
The Joshua L. Goldstein authority cites Everyday Modernity in China and identifies its author as USC faculty in modern Chinese history.

notes: Use n2006082998; n2006019059 also appears to describe the same historian. Preserve the degree-year discrepancy: AHA 1999 versus USC/LC 2000. The student-chair link is explicit.

who: Jerry B. Gough, historian of science and technology at Washington State University; PhD Cornell 1971.

evidence.says: WSU’s History Department states that Jerry Gough received his Cornell PhD in 1971, taught at WSU through 2010, and edited The Plutonium Story.
The authority links Jerry B. Gough, also Jerry Bruce Gough, to the 1971 Cornell thesis The Foundations of Modern Chemistry and to The Plutonium Story at WSU.

notes: The doctoral institution/year, WSU affiliation during 2009 and shared publication establish the match.

who: Frederick Ross (Fred R.) Gowans, historian of the western fur trade at Brigham Young University.

evidence.says: BYU’s catalogue describes a 1988 oral history in which Fred R. Gowans discusses his employment in BYU’s History Department and research on the western fur trade.
The authority gives Frederick Ross Gowans as a variant of Fred R. Gowans and identifies him as a BYU emeritus professor specializing in fur-trade and western history.

notes: The full-name variant, department and field support the match. The AHA’s BYU 1972 doctorate was not independently confirmed in the accessible sources.

who: Frank Warren Graff, historian of diplomacy at Boston College; PhD Michigan 1971.

evidence.says: The authority for Frank Warren Graff’s Strategy of Involvement identifies him as a former Boston College diplomatic-history professor with a Michigan PhD thesis from 1971.

Richard H. Immerman’s H-Diplo memoir identifies Frank Graff as his initial Boston College adviser, trained at Michigan under Bradford Perkins, and Arnold Offner as his later unofficial dissertation adviser.

notes: Institution, degree and student testimony agree. Qualify the AHA relationship: Graff was Immerman’s initial adviser; Offner subsequently advised the dissertation unofficially.
